postings.title: Facility Security Officer
postings.description:
Role overview

The Facility Security Officer (FSO) is responsible for developing, implementing, and managing the physical and cybersecurity programs for a nuclear fuel fabrication facility to protect personnel, nuclear materials, sensitive information, critical assets, and company operations. This role ensures compliance with all applicable regulatory, licensing, cyber, and company security requirements through the administration of access control programs, security procedures, threat assessments, cybersecurity governance, emergency response coordination, and security-related training. The Facility Security Officer oversees security personnel and systems, including physical security technologies, network security monitoring, cybersecurity awareness programs, and incident response activities. Working closely with operations, regulatory affairs, information technology, and site leadership, the position maintains a robust defense-in-depth security posture while fostering a culture of vigilance, accountability, and cyber awareness. The Facility Security Officer serves as a key advisor to management on security and cybersecurity matters, ensuring the protection of the facility, its workforce, digital infrastructure, and mission through continuous improvement and adherence to nuclear industry security standards and best practices.

Main activities

• Security Administration: Develop, implement, and maintain approved facility security plans, standard operating procedures, and emergency response protocols.
• Access & Clearance Management: Verify personnel security clearances, maintain access control lists, and oversee visitor control for designated classified areas.
• Information Safeguarding: Direct the secure receipt, processing, storage, transmission, reproduction, and destruction of matter containing Restricted Data.
• Compliance & Auditing:
o Conduct internal self-assessments, lead incident investigations, and facilitate mandatory DOE facility inspections and reporting.
o Conduct security and cyber vulnerability assessments, investigating physical and cyber security incidents, coordinating with Information Technology (IT) teams to protect critical systems, safeguarding sensitive and classified information,
o Implementing corrective actions to mitigate identified risks
• Training & Awareness: Deliver specialized security education and threat-awareness training to employees handling nuclear-related classified matter.

Required Qualifications

Education Experience

- Bachelor's degree in Security Management, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field.

- Equivalent combination of education, military service, law enforcement experience, or security management experience may be considered.

Experience

- 10+ years of progressively responsible experience in industrial security, nuclear security, military security, law enforcement, cybersecurity, or critical infrastructure protection.

- Experience managing physical security programs, access control systems, investigations, and emergency response.

- Experience within highly regulated industries such as nuclear, energy, defense, chemical processing, manufacturing, or government facilities preferred.

- Previous supervisory or leadership experience overseeing security personnel and contractors.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with nuclear fuel fabrication, MOX, enrichment, reprocessing, or regulated fuel-cycle facilities.

- Previous or active DOE ‘Q’ clearance

What we offer

- Salary range: $130K–$170K, commesurate with experience.

- Comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents, as well as a 401(k) plan with 4% company match.

- Generous paid time off, starting at 20 days per year and increasing to 25 days after 3 years of service.

- A mission-driven environment focused on delivering scalable, low-carbon energy solutions to meet growing global energy demand.

- A collaborative and international culture that values technical excellence, transparency, innovation, and cross-functional teamwork.

postings.title: Global Head of Cyber Security
postings.description:
The Global Head of Cyber Security is responsible for ensuring the protection and resilience of newcleo’s global technology estate, including IT, OT and critical digital assets (CDAs), across its operations in the US and Europe. The role owns the cyber security governance framework, maturity roadmap and enterprise cyber risk management required to safeguard operations, meet regulatory expectations and support business growth.

Reporting to the Head of IT RUN, the role leads the global Cyber Security function, including capability, budget and strategic suppliers, and coordinates cyber security activities across IT, Engineering and business functions. The role provides transparent reporting on cyber risk to the Head of IT RUN, with visibility to the Audit & Risk Committee, ensuring cyber risks are understood, prioritised and effectively managed across newcleo.

Main Activities

Cyber Security Governance & Framework:

- Define and maintain newcleo’s cyber security governance framework, policies, standards and maturity roadmap.

- Establish the enterprise security architecture and control framework aligned with nuclear-sector and international standards (e.g. ISO 27001, NIST CSF).

- Define and oversee core security architecture domains, including identity and access management (IAM), zero trust principles and cloud security, ensuring consistent controls across on-premise, cloud and OT environments.

- Ensure new technology, systems and digital capabilities are delivered secure by design, with security requirements embedded from project inception.

- Define cyber security priorities and investment requirements to support risk reduction, regulatory compliance and business growth.

Leadership & Team Management:

- Lead and develop the global Cyber Security function, including local security leads across key locations.

- Build capability through coaching, mentoring and succession planning.

- Manage cyber security resources, budget and strategic supplier relationships.

Security Operations & Incident Response:

- Oversee global cyber defence capabilities, including threat monitoring, vulnerability management, penetration testing and incident response.

- Lead cyber incident management, crisis response and remediation activities, coordinating with newcleo's wider business continuity and disaster recovery framework.

- Ensure appropriate security controls and monitoring across IT, OT and critical digital assets.

- Embed cyber security into operational processes and technology services.

Nuclear & Regulatory Compliance:

- Maintain alignment with relevant regulations and standards, including the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) cyber security requirements (10 CFR 73.54), French ANSSI requirements, NIS2, GDPR and IAEA nuclear security guidance.

- Support regulatory engagement and represent newcleo in cyber security audits, inspections and certifications.

- Ensure cyber security practices support nuclear safety, security and operational requirements across critical digital assets and OT environments.

Risk Management & Assurance:

- Maintain the enterprise cyber risk profile, escalating material risks, incidents and trends through appropriate governance channels.

- Provide objective challenge and assurance over the effectiveness of cyber security controls across IT, Engineering and business functions.

- Support third-party and supply chain cyber risk management, particularly for critical nuclear suppliers and partners.

Culture, Awareness & Training:

- Build a strong cyber security culture through awareness, training and targeted communications.

- Establish role-based cyber training for higher-risk functions, including Engineering, OT and Finance.

Experience

- Proven experience as a CISO / Head of Cyber Security in a global, multi-site organisation — ideally within nuclear, energy, or another critical infrastructure or highly regulated sector.

- Deep expertise across IT, OT/industrial control system (ICS/SCADA) security and critical digital assets (CDAs), ideally within a nuclear or similarly regulated environment.

- Strong track record engaging Boards, Audit & Risk Committees and regulators on cyber risk.

- Working knowledge of nuclear-sector regulatory frameworks and international standards (ISO 27001, NIST CSF).

- Experience leading incident response and crisis management at enterprise scale.

- Relevant professional certification (e.g. CISSP, CISM, CRISC) desirable.

Language Proficiency:

- Strong written and verbal communication skills in English (CEFR C1+)

- French or Italian is a plus.

What we offer

- Hybrid/Remote working. Availability to travel to the office.

- Salary range: $190K–$240K, commesurate with experience.

- Comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents, as well as a 401(k) plan with 4% company match.

- Generous paid time off, starting at 20 days per year and increasing to 25 days after 3 years of service.

- A mission-driven environment focused on delivering scalable, low-carbon energy solutions to meet growing global energy demand.

- A collaborative and international culture that values technical excellence, transparency, innovation, and cross-functional teamwork.

postings.title: Project Manager - Material Delivery & Site Readiness
postings.description:
Position Summary
The Project Manager – Material Delivery & Site Readiness will be responsible for driving the actions required to ensure timely, complete, and budget-compliant delivery of all materials, equipment, and site support packages needed for the MOX fuel fabrication project. This role will act as a key coordination point between procurement, logistics, engineering, construction, quality, and site operations to secure material readiness and avoid schedule impacts. The successful candidate will bring extensive experience in large nuclear infrastructure or fuel-cycle projects, with a strong track record in project execution, cross-functional coordination, and international collaboration.

Key Responsibilities

- Lead and coordinate all actions contributing to the on-time and on-budget delivery of materials and equipment to the construction site.

- Monitor procurement, fabrication, shipping, customs, receiving, storage, and site issue resolution.

- Track critical materials, long-lead items, and site constraints, and proactively manage risks and recovery actions.

- Coordinate with engineering, construction, logistics, suppliers, QA/QC, and project controls teams to resolve interface issues.

- Ensure material readiness aligns with the project schedule, construction priorities, and commissioning needs.

- Follow up supplier commitments, expediting actions, delivery milestones, and nonconformance resolution.

- Support budget control through delivery performance monitoring, change identification, and mitigation of cost impacts.

- Report progress, risks, and corrective actions to project leadership using structured KPI-based reporting.

- Promote a strong nuclear safety, quality, compliance, and accountability culture.

- Work effectively with U.S. and international stakeholders in a multicultural project environment.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in engineering, supply chain, construction management, project management, or a related field.

- 10+ years of experience in project execution, material delivery, logistics coordination, or project management on major infrastructure projects.

- Strong experience in nuclear construction, nuclear industrial facilities, or similarly complex regulated environments.

- Proven ability to drive delivery performance across multiple interfaces and contractor organizations.

- Strong knowledge of schedule control, issue management, expediting, and cost awareness.

- Demonstrated experience working in international and multicultural project environments.

- Excellent communication, leadership, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience in nuclear fuel fabrication, MOX, enrichment, reprocessing, or other fuel-cycle projects.

- Experience with long-lead procurement, site logistics, and construction material readiness in highly regulated industries.

- Familiarity with EPC/EPCM delivery models and nuclear quality assurance expectations.

What We Offer

• Comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents, as well as a 401(k) plan with 4% company match.
• Generous paid time off, starting at 20 days per year and increasing to 25 days after 3 years of service.
• A mission-driven environment focused on delivering scalable, low-carbon energy solutions to meet growing global energy demand.
• A collaborative and international culture that values technical excellence, transparency, innovation, and cross-functional teamwork.

postings.title: Responsable de la Sécurité des Systèmes d'Information (RSSI) (H/F)
postings.description:
À propos de newcleo

newcleo est une entreprise innovante du secteur nucléaire développant des réacteurs modulaires avancés (Advanced Modular Reactors, AMR) refroidis au plomb liquide, ainsi que du combustible nucléaire issu du recyclage des combustibles usés, dans l’objectif de fournir une énergie abondante, compétitive et bas carbone.

La société a été fondée par le physicien et entrepreneur Stefano Buono, à la suite de la cession de sa précédente entreprise – Advanced Accelerator Applications, société de médecine nucléaire cotée au Nasdaq – à Novartis pour 3,9 milliards de dollars.

Avec plus de 80 millions de dollars de chiffre d’affaires, autres produits et produits financiers en 2024, générés notamment par ses filiales, environ 780 millions de dollars de financements privés, et plus de 900 collaborateurs hautement qualifiés en Europe et aux États-Unis, newcleo a noué plus de 100 partenariats industriels et soutient sa croissance par des acquisitions ciblées et une intégration verticale d’acteurs clés de la chaîne de valeur nucléaire.

Le 27 mai 2026, newcleo a annoncé avoir conclu un accord définitif de rapprochement avec NewHold Investment Corp. III (NASDAQ : NHIC). Sous réserve de la finalisation de cette opération, newcleo deviendrait une société cotée aux États-Unis. La société issue de ce rapprochement devrait, sous réserve de la satisfaction de conditions usuelles, être cotée au Nasdaq sous le symbole boursier « NWCL » à l'issue de la clôture de la transaction, prévue au cours du second semestre 2026.

Plus d’informations : www.newcleo.com/investors

CE QUE NOUS POUVONS ACCOMPLIR ENSEMBLE

Dans un esprit start-up, au sein d'un groupe international en forte croissance, le/la Responsable de la Sécurité des Systèmes d'Information (RSSI) occupe un rôle stratégique et réglementaire pour les activités de newcleo en France.

Véritable référent(e) en cybersécurité et sécurité de l'information, vous êtes garant(e) de l'identification, de l'évaluation et de la maîtrise des risques liés aux systèmes d'information, tout en accompagnant les ambitions de développement de l'entreprise. Vous veillez à la conformité des dispositifs de sécurité avec les exigences réglementaires françaises, notamment dans le secteur nucléaire, ainsi qu'avec les standards et la gouvernance définis au niveau du Groupe.

Vous êtes responsable de l'adaptation, du déploiement et du maintien du programme local de sécurité de l'information afin d'assurer un niveau de protection adapté des actifs, applications, systèmes, infrastructures et processus de l'entreprise.

Rattaché(e) au Directeur IT France, vous évoluez au sein d'un environnement international et collaborez étroitement avec les équipes IT du Groupe à travers les différents pays.

Vos missions principales

- Identifier, évaluer et piloter les risques liés aux systèmes d'information, aux infrastructures IT/OT et aux actifs informationnels, en veillant à la mise en œuvre de mesures de protection conformes à l'appétence au risque de l'entreprise.

- Assurer une veille permanente sur les évolutions réglementaires françaises, notamment dans le domaine du nucléaire civil, ainsi que sur les nouvelles menaces cyber afin d'anticiper les risques et de proposer les actions adaptées.

- Garantir la conformité des dispositifs de sécurité avec les exigences réglementaires françaises (II 901, IGI 1300, etc.) et les politiques de sécurité du Groupe.

- Définir, adapter et déployer les politiques, standards et procédures de sécurité de l'information en garantissant leur cohérence avec la gouvernance internationale.

- Accompagner les projets métiers et IT en intégrant les exigences de cybersécurité dès leur conception et en définissant les mesures de réduction des risques nécessaires.

- Élaborer et suivre les indicateurs de performance ainsi que les reportings réguliers sur le niveau de sécurité à destination de la Direction et du RSSI Groupe.

- Participer à la définition, à la mise en œuvre et à l'amélioration continue des dispositifs de continuité d'activité et de reprise après sinistre en collaboration avec les équipes IT et cybersécurité du Groupe.

- Sensibiliser les collaborateurs aux enjeux de cybersécurité et contribuer au développement d'une véritable culture de la sécurité au sein de l'entreprise.

- Collaborer avec les équipes internationales afin de partager les bonnes pratiques, harmoniser les processus et contribuer à l'amélioration continue du programme global de cybersécurité.

NOUS IMAGINONS QUE VOUS AVEZ DÉJÀ

- Une expérience confirmée en tant que RSSI, Responsable Cybersécurité ou sur un poste similaire, dans un environnement industriel ou critique.

- Une solide expertise en gestion des risques, sécurité des systèmes d'information, cybersécurité ainsi qu'en environnements IT et OT.

- Une excellente connaissance des référentiels et normes de sécurité tels que ISO/IEC 27001, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, NIST 800-53, COBIT ou ITIL.

- Une bonne maîtrise du cadre réglementaire français applicable aux Opérateurs d'Importance Vitale et aux installations nucléaires, notamment II 901 et IGI 1300.

- Des certifications reconnues telles que CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC ou équivalent seraient fortement appréciées.

- Une excellente capacité à communiquer avec des interlocuteurs variés, aussi bien techniques que non techniques, jusqu'au niveau de la Direction.

- De solides compétences en gestion des parties prenantes et en animation de projets transverses.

- Un excellent esprit d'analyse, de synthèse et de décision, ainsi qu'une capacité à évoluer dans un environnement exigeant, international et en forte croissance.

- La capacité à gérer plusieurs sujets simultanément, à prendre des décisions dans des contextes à forte pression et à faire preuve de pragmatisme.

- Un niveau d'anglais professionnel vous permettant d'évoluer dans un contexte international ; la maîtrise de l'italien constitue un atout.

CONTEXTE DE TRAVAIL

- Poste basé à Lyon

- Déplacements éventuels en France, Italie et Europe

Innovation, passion, ambition : rejoignez newcleo et créez le monde de demain, dès aujourd’hui.

Toute candidature sera bien évidemment traitée avec une confidentialité stricte.

Ce poste est soumis à enquête administrative.
